{{short description|Certain large countable ordinal}}
In [[set theory]], the '''large Veblen ordinal''' is a specific [[large countable ordinal]] number, named after [[Oswald Veblen]]. 

There is no standard notation for ordinals beyond the [[Feferman–Schütte ordinal]] <math>\Gamma_0</math>. Most systems of notation use symbols such as <math>\psi(\alpha)</math>, <math>\theta(\alpha)</math>, or <math>\psi_\alpha(\beta)</math>, some of which are modifications of the [[Veblen function]]s to produce countable ordinals even for uncountable arguments, and some of which are [[ordinal collapsing functions]].

The large Veblen ordinal (LVO) is <math> \sup \{ \varphi (\Omega^\omega), \varphi (\Omega^{\varphi (\Omega^\omega)}), \varphi (\Omega^{\varphi (\Omega^{\varphi (\Omega^\omega)})}), \ldots \} </math>. LVO is sometimes denoted by <math>\theta(\Omega^\Omega)</math> or <math>\psi(\Omega^{\Omega^\Omega})</math>. It was constructed by Veblen using an extension of Veblen functions allowing infinitely many arguments.

LVO is the least ordinal which is not the sum of a finite number of values of the transfinite Veblen function, <math> \varphi </math>, when applied to functions of finite support from LVO to itself. Those functions are encoded as ordinals less than <math> \operatorname{LVO}^{\operatorname{LVO}} </math> ([[ordinal exponentiation]]) and <math> \Omega </math> is used as a place holder for LVO. Notice that <math> \operatorname{LVO} = \operatorname{SVO}^\operatorname{LVO} </math> is much larger than the small Veblen ordinal SVO.
